input.rationale: The bounded-liveness consequence of the configuration loss is now witnessed. Receipt f5cb1459db5e418d9a9aa6987ef76dfc (exit 0, fourteen events, no parse loss) resolves both comparisons of the authority experiment: with RestoreCommittedLogs on, the restarted single-voter node was still a Follower after the whole 1500 ms sampling window and never became leader (witness event index 11), while the identical restart without the flag reached Leader inside the same window (evaluated event index 13). Together with the earlier witnesses, the account now runs from the lost configuration to an authority transition that never happens: the node's empty configuration routes runFollower into the 'no known peers' branch and keeps quorumSize() computed from that empty configuration, so the single-voter cluster stays without a leader indefinitely rather than for a bounded interval. The two other questions are unchanged and are not restated.

investigations.question: After that restart, does the node ever regain authority within a bounded window, or does the configuration it failed to rebuild leave it permanently unable to campaign?
investigations.hypothesis: With an empty or snapshot-age configuration, runFollower takes the 'no known peers' branch and the hasVote gate never opens, so the node stays Follower and the single-voter cluster never regains a leader.
investigations.discriminator: Restart the same single-node state with the flag on and off and sample the node's state for a bounded window: the control should reach Leader, the flagged case should stay Follower.

knowledge.statement: A node restarted with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs whose rebuilt configuration is empty stays a Follower and never campaigns: the latest configuration is empty, so runFollower takes the 'no known peers, aborting election' branch and quorumSize() returns one, while the same node restarted without the flag rebuilds the committed configuration and returns to Leader.
knowledge.conditions: Single-voter configuration bootstrapped in the log, Config.RestoreCommittedLogs=true with CommitTrackingLogStore, no snapshot so the startup configuration scan starts above the committed configuration entry; observed over a 1500 ms window with a 50 ms election timeout.

gaps.question: Does the same loss of configuration occur when a snapshot exists whose configuration index is below the index of a committed LogConfiguration entry (entries in (snapshotIndex, restored commitIndex])?

interpretations.rationale: Receipt f5cb1459db5e418d9a9aa6987ef76dfc (exit 0, fourteen events, no parse loss) settles both comparisons. Comparison 0 is violated by witness event index 11: after restarting the single-voter node with RestoreCommittedLogs on and no snapshot, became_leader is false and the final state is Follower across the whole 1500 ms sampling window, with after_latest_index 0 (admission event is the matching startup_before_restart with before_latest_index 1). Comparison 1 holds at evaluated event index 13: the identical restart without the flag reports became_leader true, final state Leader and after_latest_index 1, so the difference tracks the recovery flag and not restart timing. Source mechanism: with an empty latest configuration, runFollower's first branch logs 'no known peers, aborting election' and never sets Candidate (raft.go:228-232); even if it reached the candidate path, quorumSize() would be 1 while electSelf asks only the servers in the same empty configuration, so no vote is ever counted (raft.go:1087-1094); and the configuration is empty precisely because restoreFromCommittedLogs advanced lastApplied past the committed LogConfiguration before the startup scan (api.go:604-620 and 724-754). Consequence under the witnessed conditions: a single-voter cluster that restarts with this flag never regains a leader, so all client duties that require a leader stay pending indefinitely; the pending duty is not merely delayed but has no enabled path to completion, since the node's own committed log holds the configuration it would need. The same source branch applies to a node in a larger cluster, where it would remain unable to campaign and would also compute an empty quorum, but only the single-voter case is witnessed here.
counterevidence: The flag-off control reaches Leader inside the same 1500 ms window, so the non-campaigning is not a general restart delay.

The library deliberately grants votes when the server list is empty (bootstrap affordance), which explains why such a node still answers vote requests; the witnessed defect is the state itself, not the vote-granting rule.
limitations: Only a single-voter configuration is exercised, so an election run under a stale multi-voter membership is not witnessed.
The window is bounded at 1500 ms against a 50 ms election timeout, so a much later recovery is not excluded.
The same experiment keeps no snapshot; the snapshot-age configuration variant is witnessed only through the configuration observation, not through this authority sample.

scope.description: Boot a single-voter cluster with CommitTrackingLogs, commit ten entries, shut down, restart from the same stores, then sample the node's raft state every 10 ms for a bounded 1500 ms window (ElectionTimeout is 50 ms) and report whether leadership was ever acquired. Run with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs true and false.
assumptions: A single-voter configuration normally regains leadership within a few election timeouts, which the 1500 ms window covers by a wide margin.
No snapshot exists, so the snapshot path cannot supply the configuration.
Sampling does not perturb the node; the state is read through the library's own accessor.
excluded: Multi-voter election outcomes, which the single-voter scenario cannot witness.
The startup-blocking finding, which is a separate question.

experiment.prefix: The harness boots one node with CommitTrackingLogs and RestoreCommittedLogs, applies ten commands, records the committed configuration index, shuts down, and restarts with NewRaft on the same logs, stable and snapshots stores plus a fresh inmem transport. It then polls getState() for a bounded window and emits authority_after_restart with became_leader, the final state name, the sample window and the configuration index observed after the restart; a startup_before_restart event carries the same mode identity and the pre-restart state, and no production logic is modified.
experiment.responsibility: The library owns the state a node resumes with: once a committed configuration exists in its log, a restart must not leave it permanently unable to participate, which the caller cannot repair through the public API.

comparisons.description: A single-voter cluster restarted from its own committed state is expected to regain leadership inside the bounded window; the defect prediction is that it never campaigns.
Control: the identical restart without the flag is expected to reach Leader, separating the lost configuration from any general restart delay.

knowledge.statement: At startup the in-memory configuration (r.configurations.latest/committed) is produced only by restoreSnapshot (the latest snapshot's configuration) and by the NewRaft log scan over indexes greater than max(snapshotIndex, lastApplied). With Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled, restoreFromCommittedLogs sets lastApplied to the persisted commit index before that scan, so a committed LogConfiguration entry at an index <= the restored commit index is never processed and the node keeps the snapshot configuration, or an empty configuration when no snapshot exists.
knowledge.conditions: Config.RestoreCommittedLogs=true with a LogStore implementing CommitTrackingLogStore; the persisted commit index from GetCommitIndex is at least the index of the latest committed LogConfiguration entry; no snapshot covers that entry (no snapshot at all, or snapshot.ConfigurationIndex below it).

knowledge.statement: With Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and no snapshot, NewRaft replays the committed log by pushing one fsmMutateCh message per MaxAppendEntries-sized batch before the FSM goroutine is started; when the committed backlog requires more batches than the queue's 128 slots, the send blocks and NewRaft never returns, so the node never starts.
knowledge.conditions: Config.RestoreCommittedLogs=true with a CommitTrackingLogStore, no snapshot covering the committed range, and a restored commit index whose replay needs more than 128 batches of MaxAppendEntries entries (default 64, about 8192 entries); observed for 8402 entries (132 batches) with a bounded 15 second wait, against 8002 entries (126 batches) returning in 0-3 ms.

interpretations.rationale: Source reading establishes the mechanism: NewRaft initialises configurations to its zero value, restoreSnapshot is the only producer that can supply a configuration from persistent state (api.go:655-681), and the only other producer is the startup log scan (api.go:610-613) starting at max(snapshotIndex, lastApplied)+1. restoreFromCommittedLogs (api.go:724-754) runs before that scan and calls setCommitIndex(commitIndex) then processLogs(commitIndex, nil); processLogs forwards LogConfiguration entries to the FSM (raft.go:1366-1391) and never updates r.configurations. With RestoreCommittedLogs enabled, every committed configuration entry at or below the restored commit index is therefore invisible to the node after restart. A native construction probe of a bootstrapped single node (CommitTrackingLogs, no snapshot, 10 applied entries) reproduced the predicted difference: with the flag on the event was {after_latest_index:0, after_servers:0, after_has_vote:false, after_commit_index:11, after_last_applied:11, before_latest_index:1, snapshots:0} and the library logged 'initial configuration: index=0 servers=[]'; with the flag off the same restart reported {after_latest_index:1, after_servers:1, after_has_vote:true}. The probe is construction feedback without a retained receipt, so the formal comparison is left to the submitted experiment. Consequence under the stated conditions: the restarted node's own membership view is the pre-restart snapshot value or empty, so runFollower's 'no known peers, aborting election' branch (raft.go:228-232) and the hasVote gate (raft.go:236-246) prevent it from campaigning, and quorumSize() is computed over a configuration that contradicts the committed log (raft.go:1087-1094). Counterevidence examined: a snapshot can legitimately supply the configuration (api.go:677-678) but only as of snapshot.ConfigurationIndex, which cannot cover a configuration committed after that snapshot; appendEntries processes only entries it newly appends (raft.go:1594-1621); leaderLoop only promotes latest to committed (raft.go:797-799). Limitations: the finding is scoped to the stated configuration and store conditions; the snapshot-present variant remains a registered gap; only a controller receipt can make this a completed comparison.

The retained receipt 99b89f1a9b634301a58130e5494d394f (exit 0) contains the four emitted events, and the two result events witness the predicted difference under identical inputs: event 1 (mode on, restore_committed_logs true, snapshots 0) reports after_latest_index 0, after_servers 0, after_has_vote false with after_commit_index 11 and after_last_applied 11, while event 3 (mode off) reports after_latest_index 1, after_servers 1, after_has_vote true. The admission events (0 and 2) confirm both cases started from before_latest_index 1 with one server, so the only difference is whether restoreFromCommittedLogs advanced lastApplied. Source reading explains the mechanism: NewRaft starts with an empty configurations struct, restoreSnapshot (api.go:655-681) is the only persistent-state producer of a configuration, and the startup log scan (api.go:610-613) is the only other producer but begins at max(snapshotIndex, lastApplied)+1; restoreFromCommittedLogs (api.go:724-754) runs first and sets lastApplied to the persisted commit index, so committed LogConfiguration entries at or below it are skipped, and processLogs never updates r.configurations (raft.go:1366-1391). The receipt s declared comparisons returned unknown rather than violated: the controller reported "No corresponding prerequisite events reached: mode_on/startup_before_restart" for both on-case comparisons and the analogous message for the off-case control, because the compared identity included phase and the admission events carry phase before_restart while the result events carry after_restart. That is a declaration defect, not missing evidence, so the raw observations are retained and a successor experiment with identity_fields [mode] is submitted for a fresh, complete comparison; no completed comparison is claimed here. Consequence under the stated conditions: the restarted node holds an empty (or snapshot-age) membership view, so runFollower's "no known peers, aborting election" branch (raft.go:228-232) and the hasVote gate (raft.go:236-246) leave it unable to campaign, and quorumSize() (raft.go:1087-1094) is computed over a configuration that contradicts its own committed log.
counterevidence: A restart without RestoreCommittedLogs keeps the configuration (event 3), which isolates the flagged recovery path rather than the restart itself.
A snapshot can supply a configuration (api.go:677-678), but only as of snapshot.ConfigurationIndex, which cannot cover a configuration committed after that snapshot.

interpretations.rationale: Receipt 75c355f2a4634b5193fa97e4de987fe0 (exit 0, six events, no parse loss) both repeats the first scenario and settles the registered gap. Its events 0-3 repeat the no-snapshot pair with the same values as receipt 3e2dd223dd5f43409c21066a1ca43175: mode on yields after_latest_index 0, after_servers 0 and after_has_vote false while after_commit_index 11 and after_last_applied 11 were restored, and the mode off control yields index 1 with one voter. Events 4 and 5 cover the snapshot-present case: before shutdown the log's latest configuration is index 1227 with two servers while the snapshot sits at index 1220 with configuration index 1 (one server), and after the restart the node reports after_latest_index 1, after_servers 1 and matches_committed_log false, so both declared comparisons are violated by witness event index 5 with admission event index 4. The mechanism is the one the source predicts: NewRaft starts with an empty configurations struct, restoreSnapshot (api.go:655-681) is the only persistent-state producer of a configuration, and the startup log scan (api.go:610-613) is the only other producer but begins at max(snapshotIndex, lastApplied)+1 because restoreFromCommittedLogs (api.go:724-754) has already advanced lastApplied to the persisted commit index; processLogs forwards LogConfiguration entries to the FSM without ever updating r.configurations (raft.go:1366-1391). The node therefore resumes with a membership view that its own committed log contradicts: in the witnessed case it drops a committed membership change (an added nonvoter) that postdates its snapshot, and in the no-snapshot case it resumes with no peers at all, which runFollower's 'no known peers, aborting election' branch (raft.go:228-232) and the hasVote gate (raft.go:236-246) turn into a permanent inability to campaign, with quorumSize() (raft.go:1087-1094) computed over the stale configuration. interpretations.rationale: Source: NewRaft's FSM queue is created with capacity 128 (api.go:558-561) and the FSM, main and snapshot goroutines are only started after the startup work at api.go:632-639; restoreFromCommittedLogs (api.go:724-754) calls processLogs, which pushes one message per batch of MaxAppendEntries entries into that queue (raft.go:1296-1320). A committed backlog needing more than 128 batches therefore has no consumer while NewRaft runs. A native construction probe with the default MaxAppendEntries of 64 measured a sharp boundary: 8002 committed entries (126 batches) returned from NewRaft in 3 ms, while 8402 entries (132 batches) had not returned after a bounded 15 second wait. That probe is construction feedback without a retained receipt, so the submitted experiment repeats both sizes under controller execution and only its receipt can make this a completed comparison.
counterevidence: A backlog that stays at or below the queue capacity returns promptly, so the failure is not general slowness of log replay.
limitations: No receipt yet; the account rests on source reading plus a native probe.
The interval is a bounded wait, not an infinite-run proof; a later repair or a substantially different schedule is not excluded.
The queue capacity is taken from the source constant, not measured.

interpretations.rationale: Receipt 04fccedbacf54df3b7064fd16fa57b26 (exit 0, ten events, no parse loss) witnesses the prediction: with RestoreCommittedLogs on, no snapshot, 8402 committed entries and a restored commit index of 8402 (event index 8), the restart reported newraft_returned false after a bounded 15 second wait (event index 9), so comparison 0 is violated with witness event index 9. The paired below-capacity case is retained as an observation, not as a completed comparison: event index 7 reports newraft_returned true after 0 ms for 8002 entries, but comparison 1 returned unknown because both backlog cases shared one result event name, so each comparison looked for the other case's admission and the controller marked the other result incomplete; the corrected declaration gives each size its own result event and is submitted as a successor experiment. Source mechanism: NewRaft creates fsmMutateCh with capacity 128 (api.go:558-561) and starts the FSM, main and snapshot goroutines only after the startup work at api.go:632-639, while restoreFromCommittedLogs (api.go:724-754) calls processLogs, which pushes one message per batch of MaxAppendEntries entries into that queue (raft.go:1296-1320). A replay needing more than 128 batches therefore blocks on an unconsumed channel inside NewRaft, with no retry, timeout or fallback in that path. Consequence under the stated conditions: the node never finishes starting, so a node that should resume service after a restart does not, and every duty depending on it (elections, replication, convergence) is stalled indefinitely rather than bounded; with the default MaxAppendEntries of 64 the boundary sits near 8192 committed entries and the default TrailingLogs of 10240 allows a log that large before any snapshot.
counterevidence: The sub-capacity case returned immediately (0 ms for 8002 entries), so the outcome is not general slowness of replaying committed logs.
No snapshot existed in either case, so the blocking is independent of snapshot restore.
limitations: The failing case is a bounded 15 second wait, not an infinite-run proof; a different schedule or a later repair is not excluded by this observation alone.
The queue capacity of 128 and the batch size are taken from the source, not measured.
The configuration-loss finding under the parent question is a separate defect and is not part of this account.

result.summary: The bounded-liveness consequence is now witnessed. Receipt f5cb1459db5e418d9a9aa6987ef76dfc (exit 0, fourteen events) resolves both comparisons of the authority experiment: with RestoreCommittedLogs on, the restarted single-voter node stayed Follower for the entire 1500 ms window and never became leader (violated, witness event index 11, after_latest_index 0), while the identical restart without the flag reached Leader in the same window (control holds, evaluated index 13, after_latest_index 1). The interpretation for ec0aa4e70fc945f59fb6d1ae7a1f1396-question-0 is recorded as violated with defect_claim asserted, and a Behavior knowledge entry is promoted with that execution. The chain is now: restoreFromCommittedLogs advances lastApplied past the committed configuration, NewRaft's scan therefore never rebuilds it, runFollower's no-known-peers branch and an empty quorumSize keep the node from campaigning, so a single-voter cluster that restarts with this flag never regains a leader and client duties stay pending with no enabled path to completion. Counterevidence retained: the flag-off control isolates the recovery path, and the library's deliberate vote-granting on an empty configuration explains vote answers but not the lost state. The other two questions are unchanged.

knowledge.statement: A node restarted with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs whose rebuilt configuration is empty stays a Follower and never campaigns: the latest configuration is empty, so runFollower takes the 'no known peers, aborting election' branch and quorumSize() returns one, while the same node restarted without the flag rebuilds the committed configuration and returns to Leader.
knowledge.conditions: Single-voter configuration bootstrapped in the log, Config.RestoreCommittedLogs=true with CommitTrackingLogStore, no snapshot so the startup configuration scan starts above the committed configuration entry; observed over a 1500 ms window with a 50 ms election timeout.

interpretations.rationale: Source reading establishes the mechanism: NewRaft initialises configurations to its zero value, restoreSnapshot is the only producer that can supply a configuration from persistent state (api.go:655-681), and the only other producer is the startup log scan (api.go:610-613) starting at max(snapshotIndex, lastApplied)+1. restoreFromCommittedLogs (api.go:724-754) runs before that scan and calls setCommitIndex(commitIndex) then processLogs(commitIndex, nil); processLogs forwards LogConfiguration entries to the FSM (raft.go:1366-1391) and never updates r.configurations. With RestoreCommittedLogs enabled, every committed configuration entry at or below the restored commit index is therefore invisible to the node after restart. A native construction probe of a bootstrapped single node (CommitTrackingLogs, no snapshot, 10 applied entries) reproduced the predicted difference: with the flag on the event was {after_latest_index:0, after_servers:0, after_has_vote:false, after_commit_index:11, after_last_applied:11, before_latest_index:1, snapshots:0} and the library logged 'initial configuration: index=0 servers=[]'; with the flag off the same restart reported {after_latest_index:1, after_servers:1, after_has_vote:true}. The probe is construction feedback without a retained receipt, so the formal comparison is left to the submitted experiment. Consequence under the stated conditions: the restarted node's own membership view is the pre-restart snapshot value or empty, so runFollower's 'no known peers, aborting election' branch (raft.go:228-232) and the hasVote gate (raft.go:236-246) prevent it from campaigning, and quorumSize() is computed over a configuration that contradicts the committed log (raft.go:1087-1094). Counterevidence examined: a snapshot can legitimately supply the configuration (api.go:677-678) but only as of snapshot.ConfigurationIndex, which cannot cover a configuration committed after that snapshot; appendEntries processes only entries it newly appends (raft.go:1594-1621); leaderLoop only promotes latest to committed (raft.go:797-799). Limitations: the finding is scoped to the stated configuration and store conditions; the snapshot-present variant remains a registered gap; only a controller receipt can make this a completed comparison.

The retained receipt 99b89f1a9b634301a58130e5494d394f (exit 0) contains the four emitted events, and the two result events witness the predicted difference under identical inputs: event 1 (mode on, restore_committed_logs true, snapshots 0) reports after_latest_index 0, after_servers 0, after_has_vote false with after_commit_index 11 and after_last_applied 11, while event 3 (mode off) reports after_latest_index 1, after_servers 1, after_has_vote true. The admission events (0 and 2) confirm both cases started from before_latest_index 1 with one server, so the only difference is whether restoreFromCommittedLogs advanced lastApplied. Source reading explains the mechanism: NewRaft starts with an empty configurations struct, restoreSnapshot (api.go:655-681) is the only persistent-state producer of a configuration, and the startup log scan (api.go:610-613) is the only other producer but begins at max(snapshotIndex, lastApplied)+1; restoreFromCommittedLogs (api.go:724-754) runs first and sets lastApplied to the persisted commit index, so committed LogConfiguration entries at or below it are skipped, and processLogs never updates r.configurations (raft.go:1366-1391). The receipt s declared comparisons returned unknown rather than violated: the controller reported "No corresponding prerequisite events reached: mode_on/startup_before_restart" for both on-case comparisons and the analogous message for the off-case control, because the compared identity included phase and the admission events carry phase before_restart while the result events carry after_restart. That is a declaration defect, not missing evidence, so the raw observations are retained and a successor experiment with identity_fields [mode] is submitted for a fresh, complete comparison; no completed comparison is claimed here. Consequence under the stated conditions: the restarted node holds an empty (or snapshot-age) membership view, so runFollower's "no known peers, aborting election" branch (raft.go:228-232) and the hasVote gate (raft.go:236-246) leave it unable to campaign, and quorumSize() (raft.go:1087-1094) is computed over a configuration that contradicts its own committed log.
counterevidence: A restart without RestoreCommittedLogs keeps the configuration (event 3), which isolates the flagged recovery path rather than the restart itself.
A snapshot can supply a configuration (api.go:677-678), but only as of snapshot.ConfigurationIndex, which cannot cover a configuration committed after that snapshot.
limitations: The comparison outcomes in this receipt are unknown; a completed comparison waits on the successor experiment.
Only the single-node, no-snapshot case is witnessed; the snapshot-present variant remains the registered gap.
The separate suspicion that restoreFromCommittedLogs' processLogs call can block NewRaft before runFSM starts is untested and outside this claim.

They are not fragments of one history: each receipt is a self-contained execution of the whole scenario, and the second one exists only because the comparison declaration changed (identity_fields reduced to mode); the first receipt's raw events are cited as observations, and only the second receipt's comparison outcomes are used as the completed comparison.

interpretations.rationale: Receipt 75c355f2a4634b5193fa97e4de987fe0 (exit 0, six events, no parse loss) both repeats the first scenario and settles the registered gap. Its events 0-3 repeat the no-snapshot pair with the same values as receipt 3e2dd223dd5f43409c21066a1ca43175: mode on yields after_latest_index 0, after_servers 0 and after_has_vote false while after_commit_index 11 and after_last_applied 11 were restored, and the mode off control yields index 1 with one voter. Events 4 and 5 cover the snapshot-present case: before shutdown the log's latest configuration is index 1227 with two servers while the snapshot sits at index 1220 with configuration index 1 (one server), and after the restart the node reports after_latest_index 1, after_servers 1 and matches_committed_log false, so both declared comparisons are violated by witness event index 5 with admission event index 4. The mechanism is the one the source predicts: NewRaft starts with an empty configurations struct, restoreSnapshot (api.go:655-681) is the only persistent-state producer of a configuration, and the startup log scan (api.go:610-613) is the only other producer but begins at max(snapshotIndex, lastApplied)+1 because restoreFromCommittedLogs (api.go:724-754) has already advanced lastApplied to the persisted commit index; processLogs forwards LogConfiguration entries to the FSM without ever updating r.configurations (raft.go:1366-1391). The node therefore resumes with a membership view that its own committed log contradicts: in the witnessed case it drops a committed membership change (an added nonvoter) that postdates its snapshot, and in the no-snapshot case it resumes with no peers at all, which runFollower's 'no known peers, aborting election' branch (raft.go:228-232) and the hasVote gate (raft.go:236-246) turn into a permanent inability to campaign, with quorumSize() (raft.go:1087-1094) computed over the stale configuration. Receipt 99b89f1a9b634301a58130e5494d394f is retained for its raw events only, since its comparisons could not correlate and returned unknown.

The loss therefore also occurs when a snapshot exists but predates the committed configuration change.

knowledge.assertion: Startup configuration comes only from restoreSnapshot and from the log scan above max(snapshotIndex, lastApplied), so RestoreCommittedLogs hides committed configuration entries at or below the restored commit index.

counterevidence: The control case with RestoreCommittedLogs off keeps the committed configuration in both scenarios, isolating the recovery path rather than the restart, the stores or the applied entries.
The snapshot path does supply a configuration (api.go:677-678), which is why the snapshot-present case needed a configuration change newer than the snapshot to expose the loss.
limitations: Both witnessed cases use a single voter, so consequences that require a multi-voter election (for example a node campaigning under a stale membership) are argued from the code and not witnessed.
The nonvoter addition keeps the quorum at one voter; a voter-adding change that a stale configuration would miscount is not witnessed.
The separate startup-blocking suspicion is recorded as its own question and is not part of this account.

interpretations.rationale: Source: NewRaft's FSM queue is created with capacity 128 (api.go:558-561) and the FSM, main and snapshot goroutines are only started after the startup work at api.go:632-639; restoreFromCommittedLogs (api.go:724-754) calls processLogs, which pushes one message per batch of MaxAppendEntries entries into that queue (raft.go:1296-1320). A committed backlog needing more than 128 batches therefore has no consumer while NewRaft runs. A native construction probe with the default MaxAppendEntries of 64 measured a sharp boundary: 8002 committed entries (126 batches) returned from NewRaft in 3 ms, while 8402 entries (132 batches) had not returned after a bounded 15 second wait. That probe is construction feedback without a retained receipt, so the submitted experiment repeats both sizes under controller execution and only its receipt can make this a completed comparison.
counterevidence: A backlog that stays at or below the queue capacity returns promptly, so the failure is not general slowness of log replay.
limitations: No receipt yet; the account rests on source reading plus a native probe.
The interval is a bounded wait, not an infinite-run proof; a later repair or a substantially different schedule is not excluded.
The queue capacity is taken from the source constant, not measured.

interpretations.rationale: Receipt 04fccedbacf54df3b7064fd16fa57b26 (exit 0, ten events, no parse loss) witnesses the prediction: with RestoreCommittedLogs on, no snapshot, 8402 committed entries and a restored commit index of 8402 (event index 8), the restart reported newraft_returned false after a bounded 15 second wait (event index 9), so comparison 0 is violated with witness event index 9. The paired below-capacity case is retained as an observation, not as a completed comparison: event index 7 reports newraft_returned true after 0 ms for 8002 entries, but comparison 1 returned unknown because both backlog cases shared one result event name, so each comparison looked for the other case's admission and the controller marked the other result incomplete; the corrected declaration gives each size its own result event and is submitted as a successor experiment. Source mechanism: NewRaft creates fsmMutateCh with capacity 128 (api.go:558-561) and starts the FSM, main and snapshot goroutines only after the startup work at api.go:632-639, while restoreFromCommittedLogs (api.go:724-754) calls processLogs, which pushes one message per batch of MaxAppendEntries entries into that queue (raft.go:1296-1320). A replay needing more than 128 batches therefore blocks on an unconsumed channel inside NewRaft, with no retry, timeout or fallback in that path. Consequence under the stated conditions: the node never finishes starting, so a node that should resume service after a restart does not, and every duty depending on it (elections, replication, convergence) is stalled indefinitely rather than bounded; with the default MaxAppendEntries of 64 the boundary sits near 8192 committed entries and the default TrailingLogs of 10240 allows a log that large before any snapshot.
counterevidence: The sub-capacity case returned immediately (0 ms for 8002 entries), so the outcome is not general slowness of replaying committed logs.
No snapshot existed in either case, so the blocking is independent of snapshot restore.
limitations: The failing case is a bounded 15 second wait, not an infinite-run proof; a different schedule or a later repair is not excluded by this observation alone.
The queue capacity of 128 and the batch size are taken from the source, not measured.
The configuration-loss finding under the parent question is a separate defect and is not part of this account.

knowledge.assertion: NewRaft blocks forever on an unconsumed fsmMutateCh when the RestoreCommittedLogs replay needs more batches than the queue holds.

counterevidence: The sub-capacity case returns immediately in two independent receipts (0 ms and 2 ms for 8002 entries), so the outcome is not general slowness.
No snapshot existed in either case, so the blocking is independent of snapshot restore.
limitations: The failing case is a bounded wait, not an infinite-run proof; a later repair or a different schedule is not excluded by this observation alone.
The queue capacity of 128 and the batch size of 64 are read from the source, not measured.
The failure was observed with the in-memory commit-tracking store; whether a durable store changes the size boundary is not established.

interpretations.rationale: Source: the restarted node's configuration is empty in the no-snapshot case (api.go:604-620 with restoreFromCommittedLogs at api.go:724-754), and runFollower only campaigns when hasVote holds while an empty latest configuration takes the 'no known peers, aborting election' branch (raft.go:228-246); quorumSize() would also be computed from that empty configuration (raft.go:1087-1094). A native construction probe of a single-voter cluster restarted after ten applied entries measured the predicted difference: with the flag on the node stayed Follower and became_leader was false over a 1500 ms window (ElectionTimeout is 50 ms), while the flag-off control reached Leader with after_latest_index 1. That probe is construction feedback without a retained receipt, so the submitted experiment re-runs both cases under controller execution; only its receipt can make this comparison complete.
counterevidence: The control restart reaches Leader in the same window, so the non-campaigning is not a general restart delay.
limitations: No receipt yet; the account rests on source reading plus a native probe.
Only a single-voter configuration is exercised, so election outcomes under a stale multi-voter membership are not witnessed here.
The window is bounded, so a much later recovery is not excluded.

interpretations.rationale: Receipt f5cb1459db5e418d9a9aa6987ef76dfc (exit 0, fourteen events, no parse loss) settles both comparisons. Comparison 0 is violated by witness event index 11: after restarting the single-voter node with RestoreCommittedLogs on and no snapshot, became_leader is false and the final state is Follower across the whole 1500 ms sampling window, with after_latest_index 0 (admission event is the matching startup_before_restart with before_latest_index 1). Comparison 1 holds at evaluated event index 13: the identical restart without the flag reports became_leader true, final state Leader and after_latest_index 1, so the difference tracks the recovery flag and not restart timing. Source mechanism: with an empty latest configuration, runFollower's first branch logs 'no known peers, aborting election' and never sets Candidate (raft.go:228-232); even if it reached the candidate path, quorumSize() would be 1 while electSelf asks only the servers in the same empty configuration, so no vote is ever counted (raft.go:1087-1094); and the configuration is empty precisely because restoreFromCommittedLogs advanced lastApplied past the committed LogConfiguration before the startup scan (api.go:604-620 and 724-754). Consequence under the witnessed conditions: a single-voter cluster that restarts with this flag never regains a leader, so all client duties that require a leader stay pending indefinitely; the pending duty is not merely delayed but has no enabled path to completion, since the node's own committed log holds the configuration it would need. The same source branch applies to a node in a larger cluster, where it would remain unable to campaign and would also compute an empty quorum, but only the single-voter case is witnessed here.
counterevidence: The flag-off control reaches Leader inside the same 1500 ms window, so the non-campaigning is not a general restart delay.

The library deliberately grants votes when the server list is empty (bootstrap affordance), which explains why such a node still answers vote requests; the witnessed defect is the state itself, not the vote-granting rule.
limitations: Only a single-voter configuration is exercised, so an election run under a stale multi-voter membership is not witnessed.
The window is bounded at 1500 ms against a 50 ms election timeout, so a much later recovery is not excluded.
The same experiment keeps no snapshot; the snapshot-age configuration variant is witnessed only through the configuration observation, not through this authority sample.
